title: Clear-Tape Snapshot and Head Bounds
statement: Let $d$ be a configuration of a four-work-tape machine, let $p$ be an integer, let $b,e,w$ be finite words over its symbol alphabet, and let $j_0$ be one of the four tapes. Suppose $j_0$ is tape $1$ or tape $3$, with $b=w$ if $j_0=1$ and $e=w$ if $j_0=3$. Start the tape-clearing machine on the snapshot of $d$ in phase `sweep`, with offset $p$ and buffers $b,e$. After $2|w|+2$ steps, the resulting configuration is the snapshot in phase `done` with offset $p$, with the destination buffer emptied and the other buffer unchanged. At every earlier step $u<2|w|+2$ the state is not `done`; at every step $u\le 2|w|+2$, the destination head lies in the integer interval from its position in $d$ minus $1$ through that position plus $|w|$, while every other head remains at its initial snapshot position.
hypotheses_covered: Head interval bound for the destination at every step through the run
Other heads stay fixed relative to the initial snapshot
